title: SQS accuracy-complexity trade-off in polynomial Ridge degree selection
setting: Each run draws a small regression set (first 5 features of load_diabetes, or make_friedman1 with 5 features), adds Gaussian target noise, and holds out 20% as a test set. Candidates are polynomial Ridge models of degree 1 to 7, scored by 5-fold CV RMSE on the training pool; the accuracy-only arm picks the lowest-CV-RMSE degree, while the SQS arms pick the argmax of A^w·C^(1-w), where A is normalized CV accuracy and C is normalized simplicity (fewer coefficients), and the selected model is refit on the pool and scored by test RMSE.

paper.title: Surrogate Quality Score: A Novel Composite Performance Metric for Model Selection
paper.claim: Selecting models by SQS = A^w·C^(1-w) lowers the chosen model's complexity as w decreases, while at intermediate w the held-out RMSE stays within about 5% of the accuracy-only choice.

metric.name: rmse_regret
metric.description: Relative test-RMSE increase of the selected model over the accuracy-only model on the same split: (RMSE_sel - RMSE_acc) / RMSE_acc. The accuracy-only arm is 0 by construction, so for SQS arms this is the accuracy cost of the trade-off; read it jointly with param_ratio. Diagnostics returned: param_ratio (SQS-selected / accuracy-selected coefficient count), selected_degree, test_rmse_selected, test_rmse_acc_only.

factors.name: method
factors.description: Model selection rule. accuracy_only picks the lowest 5-fold CV RMSE (baseline). sqs_w0.25 and sqs_w0.75 pick argmax A^w·C^(1-w) with accuracy weight w = 0.25 (strong pressure toward simpler models) or 0.75 (mild pressure). The paper level is sqs_w0.25; sqs_w0.75 is the milder intermediate weight. Both SQS arms share data and CV folds with the baseline.

factors.name: dataset
factors.description: load_diabetes: real low-signal data (first 5 columns, standardized target). make_friedman1: known nonlinear target with 5 features and no built-in noise.

factors.name: n_samples
factors.description: Total rows drawn per run; 20% are held out for test and the rest form the CV pool. Capped at 400 because load_diabetes has only 442 rows. Small n makes higher-degree overfitting worse, so the complexity term should matter more.

factors.name: noise
factors.description: Standard deviation of additive Gaussian noise on the target (applied in unit-sd target units for load_diabetes and in raw units for make_friedman1). Higher noise shrinks accuracy gaps between candidates, so the complexity term may dominate selection.
